diagnosis.narrative: The series is dominated by a strong upward trend (a net rise of ~20% of its level). Seasonality is strong (period 52): a repeating cycle explains much of the movement. The spectrum is close to white noise, so most of the variation is irregular and hard to predict. The series reads as stationary by the ADF/KPSS tests. Across validation windows the model ranking is unstable (Kendall tau 0.072), which favours a robust combination.

The series has strong trend and seasonality but unstable ranking; a robust trimmed_mean may reduce influence of outlier models.
Given the unstable ranking and strong trend/seasonality, try a simple unbiased mean to see if a robust baseline beats weighted combos.
Try a deterministic Bayesian averaging (dba) to exploit robust combination when ranking is unstable.
Test a simple robust median combination given unstable ranking and low predictability.
The series has unstable ranking and strong seasonality; a per‑horizon top‑k mean may capture horizon‑specific strengths.
The series has unstable ranking and strong seasonality; testing a per‑horizon weighted combo on the top‑7 models may capture horizon‑specific strengths.
The series has unstable ranking and strong trend/seasonality; a robust weighted combination on a more selective pool might improve over the full‑pool softmax that already underperforms.
Test a simple unbiased mean on the reduced, stable pool4 to see if a smaller robust set can beat dba given the unstable ranking and strong trend/seasonality.
The series has unstable ranking and strong seasonality; testing a per‑horizon one‑hot weighting may capture horizon‑specific strengths.
Test a per‑horizon weighted combo on the reduced pool4 to see if horizon‑specific strengths help, leveraging the unstable ranking and strong seasonality.

decision.justification: Selected 'dba' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.9351. Series context: trend strength 0.9999 and seasonal strength 1.0; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.072); 3 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 2.642.
